name: android-mock-location-mcp

tools.name: geo_list_devices
tools.description: List connected Android devices via ADB

tools.name: geo_connect_device
tools.description: Connect to an Android device for mock location control. Automatically starts the agent service if it is not already running.

deviceId.description: Device serial from geo_list_devices, e.g. emulator-5554

tools.name: geo_set_location
tools.description: Set device GPS to coordinates or any place name/address (geocoded via configured provider). Prefer resolving place names to lat/lng coordinates yourself and passing them directly, as the default geocoder (Nominatim) is rate-limited. To resolve a place name: use WebSearch with `site:google.com/maps/place <place name>` to find an indexed Google Maps listing, then extract coordinates from the result URL — look for the `!3d<lat>!4d<lng>` parameters (e.g. `!3d40.0080766!4d-105.2342995`), or the `@lat,lng` segment (e.g. `@40.008,-105.234`). If no Maps result is found, pass the place name or address directly to the tool and let the server geocode it. If the server geocoder also fails, do ONE targeted web search for the address/place coordinates — do not perform multiple rounds of searching.

place.description: Any place name or address, e.g. 'Uber HQ', 'Tokyo Station', '123 Main St Denver'

tools.name: geo_simulate_route
tools.description: Simulate movement along a route between two points at a given speed. Routes follow real streets via a routing provider (configurable via PROVIDER env var). Accepts place names (geocoded via configured provider) or lat/lng coordinates. If 'from' is omitted, automatically uses the current mock location, or the device's real GPS position, or asks the user for their starting location. Prefer resolving place names to lat/lng coordinates yourself and passing them directly, as the default geocoder (Nominatim) is rate-limited. To resolve a place name: use WebSearch with `site:google.com/maps/place <place name>` to find an indexed Google Maps listing, then extract coordinates from the result URL — look for the `!3d<lat>!4d<lng>` parameters (e.g. `!3d40.0080766!4d-105.2342995`), or the `@lat,lng` segment (e.g. `@40.008,-105.234`). If no Maps result is found, pass the place name or address directly to the tool and let the server geocode it. If the server geocoder also fails, do ONE targeted web search for the address/place coordinates — do not perform multiple rounds of searching.

profile.description: Routing profile. Use 'foot' for walking, 'bike' for cycling, 'car' for driving. Choose based on the user's intent.

tools.description: Test geofence enter/exit/bounce behavior at a location. Accepts place names (geocoded via configured provider) or lat/lng coordinates. place.description: Geofence center place name or address

bounceCount.description: Number of boundary crossings for bounce action

tools.name: geo_get_status
tools.description: Get current connection and simulation status

tools.name: geo_get_location
tools.description: Get the device's current real GPS location (last known position from the device's location sensors). Only needed when no mock location is active and you need the device's physical position (e.g. as a starting point for a route). If a mock location is already set, use geo_get_status instead. If the device has no recent GPS fix, the tool will fail — in that case, ask the user for their current location.
